headline: No documented interaction pathway; both open-source docs-only profiles show no shared I/O, writes, or egress, so pairwise risks are minimal.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile shows a shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or parser surface. Agent A has no I/O surfaces and agent B also has no I/O surfaces, so there is no documented path for one to inject instructions into the other.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP channel, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep both agents isolated from shared workspaces.
Disable any future clipboard or file handoff between them.
Review any added MCP or queue bridge before enabling it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents are docs-only, open-source, and show no data classes touched, no I/O surfaces, and no network egress. With no shared workspace or outbound path documented, there is no plausible leakage route between them in the provided profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is configured to read a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in any shared directory.
Keep both agents on separate local workspaces.
Audit any future upload or sync feature before use.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A is not runnable and exposes no write surfaces; agent B also has no documented write surfaces or concurrency model. Without overlapping mutable resources, there is no capability conflict to arbitrate.
conditions: IF agent B is later given write access to the same directory or database as another agent, conflict risk may emerge.
mitigations: Add locking before enabling any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The profiles do not show that agent B consumes agent A's outputs, nor that either agent takes downstream actions. Agent A is a non-runnable reference list and agent B has no documented action-taking authority, so a cascade is not evidenced.
conditions: IF agent A's outputs are later fed into agent B without verification, cascading error risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require validation of any transferred outputs.
Do not auto-chain the agents until provenance checks exist.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented in either profile. Both agents touch no data classes and have no egress, so there is no compliance breach pathway evidenced here.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's workflow, compliance review is required before deployment.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document residency and retention before any production use.
Add a compliance checklist for future integrations.
